summary: Wired's Cyber Monday 2023 roundup of Walmart deals on products its reviewers have tested, with prices based on recent street prices. It covers PC and gaming, home and kitchen, TVs and soundbars, watches and fitness trackers, headphones and earbuds, smart home gear, and speakers. Each entry gives a short verdict, often with a WIRED rating.
one_line: Wired's curated list of Walmart Cyber Monday 2023 deals on tested tech, from laptops and TVs to soundbars, earbuds and smart home devices.
key_facts: Wired says it tests products year-round and handpicked these Walmart deals; discounts are based on actual street prices at retailers over the past few months.

The Nintendo Switch OLED (8/10, WIRED Recommends) typically sells for $349; the bundle adds a digital copy of Super Smash Bros. Ultimate and a three-month Nintendo Switch Online membership, about $70 worth of extras.
The LG DualUp monitor is built to be vertical and has a 16:18 aspect ratio, and it comes with an arm mount.
The Dyson Pure Hot + Cool combines a fan, electric heater and air purifier and filters 99.97 percent of particles 0.3 microns in size.
The Samsung QN900C (8/10, WIRED Recommends) can display up to 8K resolution; the LG C3 was crowned Best TV for Gamers, with a 9.2 millisecond response time and four HDMI 2.1 ports.
The Sonos Arc (9/10, WIRED Recommends) is Wired's favorite soundbar for big home theaters, with three tweeters and eight mid-woofers and full Dolby Atmos support.
The Whoop 4 subscription costs $30 per month, but the deal includes a year.
The Ultrahuman Ring Air (7/10, WIRED Recommends) is a titanium fitness and sleep ring that needs no subscription and has a four-day battery life.
The Bose QuietComfort Ultra headphones (9/10, WIRED Recommends) arrived in October and are described as very pricey but with class-leading noise canceling.

The EufyCam 3 (8/10, WIRED Recommends) records up to 4K with 16 GB of local storage expandable to 16 TB; Wired stopped recommending Eufy cameras after security incidents but resumed testing after the company took steps to improve.
The Google Nest Cam gives only three hours of history unless you subscribe to Nest Aware, which starts at $6 per month.
The TP-Link Deco X20 is the budget pick in Wired's Best Mesh Routers guide and usually costs $160 to $180.
The Sonos Sub (Gen 3) won't pair with the Move, Roam, Port, or Connect, and this is the lowest price Wired has tracked for it.
